title: Where does three quarters times five land?
description: Three quarters is multiplied by five, and the product is placed on a number line between the two numbers. A number between zero and one and a number greater than one give a product in the middle. Keeko raises the doubt that a fraction always makes the product the smallest.
teaching_notes: One idea: when one number is between zero and one and the other is greater than one, the product is greater than the first and less than the second. Watch for students who say a fraction in the product makes it less than both numbers.

source: Multiply 3/4 × 5 and compare the product with both numbers.
video_script.why: A learner sees that the product sits between a fraction and a number greater than one when the two are multiplied.
video_script.substitution: the numbers of the book's own third situation, three quarters and five
video_script.anchor: a number line with three quarters and five marked and one as a reference
video_script.wrong_move: thinks one fraction in the product makes it less than both numbers
video_script.payoff_line: Three quarters times five is fifteen quarters, which is less than five and greater than three quarters

final_answer.spoken: fifteen quarters, which is less than five and greater than three quarters

video_script.fraction_reading: three quarters, fifteen quarters, three and three quarters
maths_rules: 3/4 is between 0 and 1 and 5 is greater than 1
3 3/4 is less than 5 and greater than 3/4
video_script.design: A number line with the product landing between the fraction and the whole number.

narration: <bookmark mark='mult'/>Step two, write five as five over one, and multiply the tops and the bottoms.
<bookmark mark='tb'/>That is three times five on top, and four times one below.

narration: <bookmark mark='cmp2'/>Step three, compare. Fifteen quarters is the same as three and three quarters.
<bookmark mark='less'/>Three and three quarters is less than five.
<bookmark mark='more'/>It is also greater than three quarters.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 3/4 × 5 = 15/4, less than 5 and greater than 3/4
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Three quarters times five is fifteen quarters, which is less than five and greater than three quarters.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble puts the product before three quarters
marks.slip: five is marked as a large number on the line
marks.fix: the product moves to its place beyond three quarters

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one number is a fraction, so the product is less than both numbers.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>But three quarters of five is a big share of five.
It is much more than three quarters of a whole.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A number greater than one makes the product greater than the fraction.
